title: Chapter 3 — Kemi's Mother
description: Kemi's mother arrives from Ibadan without warning. She thinks her daughter works at a "hotel reception". Technically, she does.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Tuesday, 10 a.m. A woman in a church wrapper is standing at the gate with a basket of agege bread and a photograph of Kemi in her secondary school uniform.

beats.speaker: mamaKemi
beats.text: Good morning. Please, is this Sugar Hotel? My daughter Kemi works here at reception. I came to surprise her. (She looks at the bar, the stairs, the sign that says NO FIGHTING.) It is... a lively hotel.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Kemi is looking at you. Her mother is looking at you. The stairs are looking at everybody.

options.text: "Kemi is my receptionist and my accountant. The best I've had." Show her the books Kemi keeps.
Take her mother aside. Tell her the truth, gently, woman to woman.
Say nothing. Let Kemi decide what to say.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She wants to see "the hotel kitchen". Then the Friday orders start coming in, and she stands in the doorway and watches you cook for a full house.

won.toast: She eats a bowl standing up. "This is how my mother made it," she says, and then she cries a little, and blames the pepper.

lost.toast: "It is a busy kitchen," she says politely, looking at the burnt pot.

beats.speaker: mamaKemi
beats.text: (later, over pepper soup, quietly) My blood pressure. The doctor wants me on new drugs, ₦18,000 a month. Kemi sends ₦10,000. I didn't want to tell her the rest.

beats.speaker: mamaKemi
beats.text: (She hasn't touched the soup.) You told me the truth about this place. Nobody in Ibadan would believe me. (She looks at the stairs a long time.) Is my daughter safe here?

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Kemi is in the kitchen pretending not to listen.

options.text: Pay for six months of her drugs.
Give Kemi a raise so she can pay it herself.
"Lagos is hard for all of us, Mama."

beats.speaker: kemi
beats.text: (at the gate, watching her mother's bus go) She said, "Your madam is a good woman." (A pause.) She didn't say "good hotel". She's not stupid, Mama.

variants.text: (at the gate, watching her mother's bus go) I told her I do the accounts. It's true. I just didn't say for what. (She laughs, almost.) Thank you for letting me choose.

beats.title: Kemi's Mother
beats.summary: A mother came to see her daughter's "hotel". What she saw depended on you.
